inp.lead: Enter your birth date, marriage date and account opening date to get your Korean housing subscription score (out of 84), plus next year's score and special supply eligibility.
inp.refHint: Scores are counted as of the recruitment announcement date. Leave today's date if unsure.
inp.marriageHint: Leave blank if single. If you married before 30, the homeless period starts from the marriage date.
inp.neverOwned: No household member has ever owned a home
inp.disposalHint: Enter the latest date any household member sold a home.
inp.under30: Single and under 30, so the homeless period scores 0. It starts at 2 points on {date}.
inp.spouse: Spouse (counts even with a separate registration)
inp.baby: Has a child under 2 (newborn special supply)
inp.dependentsHint: {n} dependents (excluding you). Unmarried children 30+ need 1+ year on the same registry; parents who own a home are excluded.
inp.spouseSubHint: 50% of the spouse's period is added, up to 3 points. Leave blank if none.

bench.desc: A {size}-person household can reach {max} points; you have {score}. Dependents are fixed by headcount, so among same-size households the homeless and account periods decide.

special.title: Special supply quick check

newlywed.name: Newlyweds
newlywed.req: Married within 7 years (incl. engaged couples, single parents of children 6 or under), homeless, income/asset limits. Since 2024-03-25 the spouse's pre-marriage history is ignored.

firstHome.name: First home
firstHome.req: No household member has ever owned a home, 1st priority, 5+ years of income tax, income limits. Private units up to 85㎡.

newborn.name: Newborn
newborn.req: Household with a child under 2 as of the announcement. Since 2026-06-15 private housing also sets aside 10% of special supply regardless of marriage length.

multiChild.name: Multi-child
multiChild.req: 2+ minor children (incl. unborn). Private housing lowered from 3 to 2 children in 2024.

elderly.name: Elderly parent support
elderly.req: Homeless head of household supporting a parent aged 65+ for 3+ years.

special.note: Basic requirements only. Check income/asset limits, account priority and past win history in the announcement.

ratio.title: Point vs lottery ratio (private housing)
ratio.desc: Within one complex the share selected by points depends on unit size. With a low score, target sizes with a larger lottery share.
notes: Basis: Rules on Housing Supply, Art. 28 (ratios since the 2023-04-01 reform). The announcement is final.

Since 2025-10-16 (10·15 measures), all of Seoul and 12 Gyeonggi areas (Gwacheon, Gwangmyeong, Seongnam Bundang/Sujeong/Jungwon, Suwon Yeongtong/Jangan/Paldal, Anyang Dongan, Yongin Suji, Uiwang, Hanam) are regulated areas, and Hwaseong Dongtan, Yongin Giheung and Guri were added on 2026-07-01. Designations can change.
In regulated areas, the capital region and metro cities, 75%+ of lottery units go to homeless applicants first.
If you lose in the point pool, you are automatically entered into the lottery pool of the same complex.

rules.title: Homeless period (max 32)
items: Counted from your 30th birthday, or from marriage registration if you married before 30
Single and under 30: 0 points; homeowners: 0 points
Under 1 year 2 points, +2 per year, 15+ years 32 points
If you sold a home, counting restarts from the date you became homeless (whole household)

rules.title: Dependents (max 35)
items: A spouse counts even with a separate registration
Parents/grandparents (incl. in-laws) count if you are head of household and share the registry for 3+ years; excluded if either owns a home
Unmarried children count; those 30+ need 1+ year on the same registry

rules.title: Account period (max 17)
items: Under 6 months 1, 6–12 months 2, then +1 per year, 15+ years 17
50% of the spouse's period adds up to 3 points (17 cap, since 2024-03-25)
Converted legacy accounts keep the original opening date
Up to 5 years opened as a minor are recognized (2024 change)

items.q: When does the homeless period start?
items.a: On your 30th birthday, or on the marriage registration date if you married earlier. If you sold a home, the later of that date and the date you became homeless applies. It is judged for the whole household.

items.q: Is it really 0 points if I'm single and under 30?
items.a: Yes. It starts at 2 points on your 30th birthday and rises 2 points a year.

items.q: How do parents count as dependents?
items.a: You must be head of household and share the resident registry with them for 3+ consecutive years. If either parent owns a home, both are excluded. Since 2025, health insurance usage records (3 years for parents, 1 year for children aged 30+) must be submitted to prove actual residence. An April 2026 proposal would raise the same-registry requirement for unmarried children aged 30+ from 1 to 3 years — check the announcement.
Since 2024-03-25, 50% of the spouse's period is converted and added up to 3 points, capped at 17 in total. E.g. own 5 years (7) + spouse 4 years (3) = 10.

items.q: Does a small home count as homeless?
items.a: For private general supply only, one home of 60㎡ or less valued at KRW 160M or less (capital region) or KRW 100M (elsewhere) is treated as homeless. Not for special supply.
Since 2024-03-25, the longer account holder wins; if still tied, a lottery decides.
No. National housing general supply uses deposit amount/count, not points. Points apply to private housing.
